elements.label: Figure 1.5
elements.description:
Line chart of poverty rate (%) by region, 2010 to 2020, with y-axis 0 to 50 and x-axis years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020. Legend: Central Highlands (teal), Northern & Coastal Center (yellow), Midlands & Northern Mountains (gray), Mekong Delta (orange), Red River Delta (blue), Southeast (green). Printed values:

| Region | 2010 | 2012 | 2014 | 2016 | 2018 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central Highlands | 29.6 | 25.8 | 27.6 | 20.4 | 19.7 | 17.1 |
| Midlands & Northern Mountains | 39.9 | 34.0 | 32.8 | 23.4 | 22.0 | 16.0 |
| Northern & Coastal Center | 18.6 | 13.6 | 12.1 | 9.0 | 6.2 | 4.7 |
| Mekong Delta | 14.3 | 11.5 | 6.8 | 4.5 | 2 | 3.7 |
| Red River Delta | 8.6 | 4.8 | 3.6 | 1.4 | 1.2 | 0.6 |
| Southeast | 5.3 | 3.0 | 2.3 | 0.4 | 0.4 | not printed |

All series decline overall, with the Midlands & Northern Mountains starting highest at 39.9 and the Red River Delta and Southeast lowest by 2016 and after; the Southeast 2020 value is not labeled. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS.

elements.label: Figure 1.6
elements.description:
Grouped bar chart of number of poor (in millions, $3.20/day 2011PPP) by region, y-axis 0 to 6. Groups are regions; bars within each group are years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020 (legend shades from dark to light teal). No values are printed, so approximate readings:

| Region | 2010 | 2012 | 2014 | 2016 | 2018 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central Highlands | ~1.6 | ~1.4 | ~1.6 | ~1.4 | ~1.35 | ~1.0 |
| Mekong Delta | ~2.45 | ~2.05 | ~1.2 | ~0.85 | ~0.35 | ~0.65 |
| Midlands & Northern Mountains | ~4.85 | ~4.4 | ~4.05 | ~3.35 | ~3.35 | ~2.1 |
| Northern & Coastal Center | ~3.4 | ~2.6 | ~2.3 | ~1.9 | ~1.4 | ~0.95 |
| Red River Delta | ~1.6 | ~0.98 | ~0.7 | ~0.32 | ~0.27 | ~0.18 |
| Southeast | ~1.02 | ~0.65 | ~0.5 | ~0.15 | ~0.1 | ~0.1 |

The Midlands & Northern Mountains has the largest number of poor in every year, and most regions show declining counts over time. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010–2020.
